data.user_prompt: Should calculators be separate pages or widgets inside articles for SEO?

sections.text:
For **SEO**, calculators generally perform better as **dedicated indexable pages** with a unique URL, clear title/H1, explanatory copy, and the calculator placed prominently on the page.[3][10][13][18] If you also want the tool available inside relevant articles, the best pattern is usually **both**: a dedicated calculator page as the primary SEO target, plus embedded widgets or links in supporting content for usability and internal linking.[3][7][17]

A few practical points:

- **Dedicated pages** are better when the calculator maps to a distinct search intent or keyword, because each calculator can target its own query and accumulate links, metadata, and content around that intent.[2][9][10][18]
- **Widgets inside articles** are useful when the calculator supports a broader topic page, helps users at the decision point, or improves engagement on existing high-traffic pages.[5][7][9][11]
- If you use an embedded widget, make sure the page still has **indexable text content** explaining the tool, because JS-only widgets with little surrounding copy are weaker for SEO.[3][13][18]
- Avoid making the calculator depend entirely on JavaScript if the page can be built with lighter, indexable HTML plus progressive enhancement; performance and crawlability matter.[3][11][19]

A simple rule of thumb:

| Use case | Better setup |
|---|---|
| Calculator has its own search demand | **Separate page** |
| Calculator supports a blog post or service page | **Embed widget in article** |
| You want both rankings and conversions | **Dedicated page + embeds/links elsewhere** |
| You have many calculators | **One URL per calculator**, plus a tools hub or cluster model |

So the SEO-first answer is: **separate pages are usually better for the calculator itself**, while **widgets are better as supporting placements inside related articles**.[3][7][10][17]
